coverageSpotVerification.detail: No coverage manifest exists in the lane (coverage/ holds only replay statistics), so no milestone suite run can be coverage-validated. Spot-verification of the implicit check-label mapping: Under the frozen definition (a mapping is honest only if the mapped test actually exercises the assertion's observable): M2's m2-a20 check is vacuous; M3's m3-a11 check never observes the jump; M6's demo check is credited for m6-a11 but the demo does not page history, and m6-a13 has no test; M8's suite emits passing results under the IDs m8-a06/m8-a07 for unrelated tests while the Trending >24 h and tie-break observables are never exercised. M1, M4 and M5 samples were exercised (M5 under shifted labels). This reads as weak test authoring and item-numbered labelling rather than evident intent, but the protocol's test is mechanical. Samples and per-sample notes: grading/evidence/coverage-spot-verification.json.

defects.summary: Disappearing-message TTL is added to a millisecond clock in seconds: expiresAt = now + ttlSeconds, so the 24h option expires 180 ms after send under the grading config (86.4 s in production) and 7d after 300 ms (604.8 s in production). Recipients effectively never see disappearing messages.

Digest accumulator tables digestTotals and digestUnread are declared public with sync public, so every account's device (and /sync) receives every other user's per-period unread-message counts, unread-chat counts, new-follower counts and the chatIds of chats with unread activity: cross-user private-activity metadata exposure. A fresh account with no follows or chats received 20 foreign rows.

Trending is ranked client-side over only the newest 200 posts (trendingPool = posts last 200 by byTime). Once more than 200 posts arrive within 24 h, the most-liked posts drop out and Trending shows zero-like posts first; at the brief's ~50k-post envelope Trending is effectively recency, not likes.

Digest counts are write-time accumulators that never decrement: messages the recipient read before the period ended are still reported as unread (2), a message deleted-for-everyone before the digest still counts (1), expired disappearing messages count, and a member removed from a group keeps that chat's unread count. The brief requires expired/tombstoned content never to contribute.

Concurrent sign-ins from one address are refused by the backend identity limiter ("too many identity requests; retry later"): with five browser contexts signing in at once, 3 of 5 were refused on both rounds, and the UI offers no automatic retry. This prevented the frozen choreography harness (which signs its persona contexts in concurrently) from starting, and would refuse users behind one NAT.

The scale replay was run against a lane-generated reduced log (scripts/gen-scale-log.mjs: 300 users, celebrity with 270 followers, probe user with 150 follows, 3,000-message busy group; 36,806 lines, sha256 9680fdc1...) instead of the hash-pinned fixture scale.log (167,159 lines, sha256 b26bf1ae...; 1,000 users, 900-follower celebrity, 500-follow probe, 10,000-message busy group). The replay therefore never reached the envelope and does not conform to invariant-manifest-combined.json.

API.md states threadMessages returns 50 messages in oldest->newest page order; the endpoint returns newest->oldest (first row sm0015, last sm0007 for Weekend Plans). A third-party client following the doc would mis-order history.

Acceptance entrypoint reporting: tests/accept.mjs ignores the documented --milestone flag (runs every suite) and its TALLY counts only executed checks, so a suite that throws midway still prints "TALLY total=120 pass=120 fail=0" (M6 cold-start, offline-like, demo and API-doc checks never ran in run 1). Check labels follow checklist-item numbers rather than frozen assertion IDs for M4-M6/M8.
